data.source_period: 2019 guideline publication; current ACR narrative inspected 2026-10-10.

data.quantity: Appropriate next imaging options when radiographs are negative/equivocal but suspicion remains
data.source_evidence_basis: ACR Variant 2 rates each of these three options usually appropriate; they are alternatives for the next imaging study.
data.limitations: Guidance does not prescribe one modality for every patient or set a universal immobilization rule. The 10-14 day option applies to the imaging interval, not an assured appointment or diagnosis time.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Authored branch: if initial films are negative/equivocal and examination still supports fracture, keep occult fracture unresolved and present imaging/follow-up choices for clinician selection; do not convert a negative film into a definitive no-fracture result.

data.source_title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Acute Hand and Wrist Trauma
data.locator: Variant 2 narrative discussion of repeat radiographs after negative films.
data.source_setting: American College of Radiology imaging guidance; clinically suspected hand/wrist fracture.
data.source_period: 2019 guideline publication; current ACR narrative inspected 2026-10-10.
data.source_n: Guideline synthesis; no single cohort denominator.
data.quantity: Tradeoff stated for waiting for repeat radiographs
data.value: Immobilize in a short arm cast and repeat radiographs after 10-14 days is one option; delayed diagnosis may lead to functional impairment.
data.source_evidence_basis: ACR narrative describes short-arm casting with repeat films as an option and notes the potential functional cost of delayed diagnosis.
data.limitations: This statement describes an option and potential downside, not comparative event rates or a quantified impairment risk. It is broad hand/wrist evidence rather than a patient-specific prescription.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Authored branch: allow delayed repeat films only as a clinician-selected pathway with a documented plan; record the possibility of earlier CT/MRI consideration without inventing urgency thresholds.
